eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Five
subtitle: Lesson 41 · Grouping and Aggregating

eyebrow: CUBE gives you everything, whether you want it or not
code:
-- CUBE: four levels for two columns, including a
-- Size-alone subtotal you might not want here.
SELECT Color, Size, SUM(ListPrice) AS TotalListPrice
FROM Production.Product
GROUP BY CUBE (Color, Size);
caption: CUBE's full power set isn't always the report you need.

eyebrow: Say exactly which combinations you want
code:
SELECT Color, Size, SUM(ListPrice) AS TotalListPrice,
       COUNT(*) AS ProductCount
FROM Production.Product
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (
    (Color, Size),
    (Color),
    ()
);
caption: Three grouping sets, exactly: detail, Color subtotal, grand total.

eyebrow: GROUPING_ID() still works the same way
code:
SELECT Color, Size, SUM(ListPrice) AS TotalListPrice,
       GROUPING_ID(Color, Size) AS SubtotalLevel
FROM Production.Product
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (
    (Color, Size), (Color), ()
)
ORDER BY GROUPING_ID(Color, Size);
caption: Same mechanism as ROLLUP/CUBE — sort by subtotal level.

eyebrow: ROLLUP and CUBE are shorthand for this
caption: GROUPING SETS is the one notation that can reproduce either.

subtitle: Pulling every tool from this chapter into one real report.
